subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry policy fields and `cron add/edit` flags on top of the existing global `cron.retry` behavior, and what exact count/delay/backoff semantics should be public?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix because it creates a new public CLI/API/storage contract and policy interaction with the already-shipped global retry mechanism.

options.title: Approve additive per-job retry policy
options.body: Define job-local retry fields plus CLI flags that override or inherit global `cron.retry`, then require schema, storage, docs, and upgrade tests before merge.

options.title: Keep global retry only
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers decide global transient retry/backoff is the only supported scheduler policy for now.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Defer per-job knobs and track retry policy under the broader reason-aware cron guardrail work instead.

recommendation.title: Approve additive per-job retry policy
recommendation.body: Define job-local retry fields plus CLI flags that override or inherit global `cron.retry`, then require schema, storage, docs, and upgrade tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected to the merged recurring retry behavior and the current partial implementation boundary.
